speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) what is the estimated amount of energy that we will be using in the next 10 years; (b) whether our energy efficiency will be adequate to meet our future needs; (c) what measures does the Ministry have to ensure or improve energy efficiency; and (d) whether there are plans to engage in new energy sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Promoting more efficient use of energy is a key prong of our energy strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: It will reduce our carbon footprint and enhance Singapore's energy security and economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The Government has thus adopted a mix of regulations, incentives and capability-building measures to encourage energy efficiency improvements in the industrial, building and household sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: However, there is room for us to improve our energy efficiency, so as to fulfil our pledge under the Paris Agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The price signal from the carbon tax will incentivise the adoption of more energy-efficient practices by the industry, as well as the rest of the economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Capability building efforts include the Energy Efficiency Fund administered by the NEA which provides support for companies to undertake design reviews, energy audits and equipment retrofits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The EDB supports energy efficiency initiatives in the manufacturing sector through various incentives, such as the Productivity Grant, Investment Allowance, as well as energy efficiency financing programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Small and medium-sized enterprises can tap on SPRING's Capability Development Grant to adopt energy-efficient solutions that can help improve their business capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: We also aim to build up a strong pool of energy efficiency expertise in Singapore, for instance, through the Singapore Certified Energy Manager programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: In the building sector, the Government has been driving the shift towards more environmentally sustainable buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: As of January this year, there are close to 3,000 Green Mark building projects in Singapore, which is approximately one-third of the total building stock.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: For households, the Government has sought to raise awareness of energy-efficienct products through the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: In addition, inefficient household appliances are weeded out from the market through MEPS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: As a result, the average energy efficiency of refrigerators has improved by about 26% since 2008.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: To encourage households to be more energy efficient, new features, such as peer comparison, have been introduced to residential consumers' utilities bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Among alternative energy options, solar photovoltaic (PV) currently has the greatest potential for wider deployment in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Looking beyond 2020, we plan to further raise the adoption of solar power in our system to one gigawatt peak (GWp).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: We will increase solar adoption by investing in research, development and demonstration (RD&D) in solar PV and related energy technologies; addressing market barriers to deployment; enhancing our regulatory framework; and by taking the lead through aggregation of demand from public agencies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With regard to what she has mentioned earlier about energy efficiency and energy adequacy and diversification, does that take into consideration the latest CFE strategies where the latest push towards Smart Nation and digitalisation and, of course, the increase in technology would actually increase demand for energy?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Does that incorporate into our baseline in terms of energy needs over the next decade or more going forward, given the intensity of digitalisation on any usage of energy?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Under the CFE, productivity is a very important element and, by enabling our industry across sectors to achieve greater productivity, this also takes into account energy efficiency.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, we are all moving in the same broad general direction.
